very good.comment: Verbal rating of an Abitur grade of 1.0–1.5 (German sehr gut), shown in brackets after the number.

good.comment: Verbal rating of an Abitur grade of 1.6–2.5 (German gut), shown in brackets after the number.

satisfactory.comment: Verbal rating of an Abitur grade of 2.6–3.5 (German befriedigend), shown in brackets after the number.

sufficient.comment: Verbal rating of the lowest passing Abitur grades (German ausreichend), shown in brackets after the number.

très bien.comment: French Baccalauréat mention for an average of 16 or more out of 20 (“with highest honours”). Shown in brackets after the number.

bien.comment: French Baccalauréat mention for an average of 14–15.9 out of 20 (“with honours”). Shown in brackets after the number.

assez bien.comment: French Baccalauréat mention for an average of 12–13.9 out of 20 (“with fair honours”). Shown in brackets after the number.

passable.comment: French Baccalauréat: a pass without a mention (average under 12 out of 20). Shown in brackets after the number.

%@/20 (%@).comment: A French Baccalauréat average out of 20 with its mention in brackets, e.g. “15.8/20 (bien)”. First is the number, second the mention.

%lld/100.comment: An Italian maturità score out of 100, e.g. “85/100”.

%@ of 5.comment: A Japanese school record average on the five-point scale, e.g. “4.4 of 5”.

%lld/200.comment: A Ukrainian national multi-subject test (NMT) score out of 200, e.g. “185/200”.

%@/%lld.comment: A grade over its maximum, e.g. “620/750” or “16.5/20”. First is the grade, second the maximum possible.

%@ (1 = best).comment: A grade on a scale where 1 is the best, e.g. “3.0 (1 = best)”. The number is the grade.

%@ (%@).comment: A school grade followed by its letter or verbal rating in brackets, e.g. “3.4 (B+)” or “1.6 (good)”. First is the grade, second the rating.

CPA.comment: Training: Certified Public Accountant, a US accounting licence. Abbreviation (CPA); use the local equivalent title if there is one.

Board Certification.comment: Training: specialty board certification for physicians after residency (US medical system).

Pharmacy Technician.comment: Training: registered pharmacy technician (works under a pharmacist, no doctorate).

Driver's License.comment: Training: the ordinary car driving licence (US spelling “License”, US Class D).

CDL.comment: Training: Commercial Driver's License, US licence to drive trucks and buses for work. Abbreviation (CDL).

Pilot.comment: Training: private pilot licence (flying small planes, not for pay). Short name of the licence, not the job title.

Commercial Pilot.comment: Training: commercial pilot licence (flying for pay). Short name of the licence, not the job title.

LPN.comment: Training: Licensed Practical Nurse, a US nursing licence below registered nurse (RN). Abbreviation (LPN).

Nurse License.comment: Training: licence to work as a registered nurse (RN).

Nurse Practitioner.comment: Training: advanced-practice nursing licence (US): an RN who may diagnose, treat and prescribe.

Medical License.comment: Training: licence to practise medicine as a physician (US spelling “License”).

Dental License.comment: Training: licence to practise dentistry (US spelling “License”).

Pharmacist License.comment: Training: licence to practise as a pharmacist (US spelling “License”).

Veterinary License.comment: Training: licence to practise veterinary medicine (US spelling “License”).

Electrician License.comment: Training: journeyman electrician licence (US trades system; US spelling “License”).

Plumber License.comment: Training: journeyman plumber licence (US trades system; US spelling “License”).

Bar Admission.comment: Training: admission to the bar, the licence to practise as a lawyer (US, state by state).

Professional Engineer.comment: Training: Professional Engineer (PE) licence, a US state licence to sign off engineering plans.

Architect Licence.comment: Training: state licence to call yourself an architect and stamp building plans.

Pesticide Applicator.comment: Training: government permit to apply restricted-use pesticides (US-style certification).

Security Guard Licence.comment: Training: state licence to work as a security guard.

Master Electrician License.comment: Training: senior electrician licence above journeyman (US trades system).

Master Plumber License.comment: Training: senior plumber licence above journeyman (US trades system).

ATP.comment: Training: Airline Transport Pilot certificate, the highest US pilot certificate. Abbreviation (ATP).

A&P Certificate.comment: Training: Airframe & Powerplant mechanic certificate (US FAA). Abbreviation (A&P).

Police Academy.comment: Training: recruit training that qualifies you to be sworn in as a police officer.

Psychologist License.comment: Training: state licence to practise psychology (US spelling “License”).

Physical Therapy License.comment: Training: state licence to practise physical therapy (US spelling “License”).

EPA 608.comment: Training: US EPA Section 608 certification for handling refrigerants. Proper name, US-specific.

Game Development Program.comment: Training: a course in game design and programming.

Product Design Certificate.comment: Training: a UX and product-design certificate.

Music Production Certificate.comment: Training: a course in recording, mixing and producing music.

Arts & Minds.comment: Activities tab: creative and mental disciplines such as music, chess and coding

Study.comment: Activities tab: school subjects such as maths and science

Beginner.comment: Activity level after the first year of practice

Intermediate.comment: Activity level after two to three years of practice

Advanced.comment: Activity level after four to six years of practice

Expert.comment: Activity level after seven or more years of practice

Athletic.comment: Kind of contest: a sports event

E-Sports.comment: Kind of contest: a competitive video-gaming tournament | Sport: competitive video gaming

Creative.comment: Kind of contest: an arts prize

Mind.comment: Kind of contest: a contest of the mind such as chess or debate

Academic.comment: Kind of contest: a school-subject olympiad or fair

activity.science.comment: School subject (the field of work is a different key)

%@ in %@.comment: A vocational qualification under the country’s own name, followed by its field of study, e.g. “Ausbildung in Health”. The first placeholder is the local name of the qualification, the second the field.
